children: Shares of city gas distribution (CGD) companies, particularly Indraprastha Gas (IGL) and Mahanagar Gas (MGL), are in focus after the government revised the allocation mechanism for high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) gas.
The revised formula is expected to improve access to relatively cheaper gas for larger CGDs and could support sector margins, according to analysts who track the space.

Under the new methodology, CGDs facing a shortfall in CNG and domestic PNG supplies will be eligible for higher HPHT gas allocations. The shortfall will be calculated after accounting for their existing allocations and utilisation of APM gas, non-APM gas and New Well Gas (NWG).
The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG) will provide company-wise gas consumption and utilisation data for determining the allocations.

The change is significant for CGDs as HPHT gas is considerably cheaper than spot LNG. APM gas is priced at around $7 per MMBtu, HPHT gas at around $8.9 per MMBtu, while spot LNG costs around $24 per MMBtu. Higher HPHT allocations could therefore reduce CGDs' dependence on expensive spot LNG.

Previously, available HPHT gas volumes were distributed equally among all eligible bidding CGDs, rather than in proportion to their actual requirements. As a result, smaller CGDs could receive the same allocation as larger players despite having lower gas requirements.

Under the revised formula, HPHT gas allocation will be linked to a CGD's absolute requirement. This is calculated as the shortfall between its CNG and domestic PNG consumption and its utilisation of APM and NWG gas in the preceding quarter.
Citi believes the revised methodology better aligns allocations with actual gas requirements and should improve access to cheaper gas for large CGDs.

The brokerage added that retail price hikes implemented by CGDs are likely to support margins and, along with the revised gas allocation mechanism, the sector is well positioned from a medium-term perspective.
Citi's preferred stocks across the gas value chain, in order, are MGL, IGL, GAIL, Gujarat Energy (Gujarat Gas) and Petronet LNG.

Shares of Mahanagar Gas, GAIL, Gujarat Energy and Petronet LNG were trading higher on Monday, while Indraprastha Gas was down, having outperformed last week. MGL shares were trading just above the flat line, while those of GAIL rose 1.7%, Gujarat Energy advanced 0.3%, and Petronet LNG was up 1.3%. IGL, the underperformer, traded 1.61% lower.

title: High Pressure, High Temperature Gas allocation norms revised: Here are the stocks that benefit
